transcript: We Had A World is playwright Joshua Harmon's life on a plate and the perfect vehicle for Andrew Barth Feldman, Joanna Gleason, and Jeanine Serralles. This autobiographical new play tells a retrospective on Joshua's relationship with his grandmother, told through the perspectives of himself, his grandmother, and his mother, who had a very different relationship with his grandmother. This personal and reflective piece flows like a memoir as it chronicles a number of key memories, mostly chronologically, all of which were foundational to Joshua's upbringing and his understanding of his family. Through this lens, we learn how his family dynamic evolved, and how three people involved in the same situations can have completely different experiences. There's a lot of direct narration in this, which doesn't tend to be my thing, but it works for me here — the writing didn't feel stiff or formal in a way that would otherwise make me feel detached, and the pacing was very good. For performances,I was really impressed by the level of nuance and complexity that Jeanine Serralles brings to the role of Joshua's mother. You can see her among a trio of great performances at New York City Center through April 27th. With that, another playbill for my collection.
